# 08-fresco — sources

Back-test entry `08-fresco.yaml`: Fresco, the AI scribe for construction superintendents (YC Fall 2024).
Written 2026-10-22 from public material only. Quotes are verbatim from the page named; "Author's choice" marks the
smallest plausible choice made where the public material is silent.

Main sources:
- [HN] Launch HN: Fresco (YC F24), 2024-11-21 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=42204939
- [LYC] Launch YC: Fresco, the scribe for construction, 2024-10-23 — https://www.ycombinator.com/launches/M73-fresco-the-scribe-for-construction
- [YCP] YC company page — https://www.ycombinator.com/companies/fresco (now "AI-powered takeoff and estimating for Division 8 construction")
- [KOE] A contractor's daily-log expectations on Procore's support site — https://support.procore.com/tc/Koester/Site_Map/Koester_Expectations_-_Daily_Logs
- [SWI] Swiftask, Procore daily reports page (vendor) — https://swiftask.ai/ai-integration/procore/intelligent-daily-reports
- [BLS] BLS Occupational Outlook, construction managers — https://www.bls.gov/ooh/management/construction-managers.htm
- [OPU] Launch HN: Opusense (field reports for site inspectors), 2025-05-20 — https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=44042791

## The eight founder-emulation items

1. **Who.** Construction superintendents on commercial jobs.
   [HN] "Superintendents are the busiest and most expensive people on construction sites."
   [LYC] "That’s the reality for 210k+ construction superintendents (or supervisors, foremen, PMs, etc.) across the USA."
   → `roles[superintendent]`, `context.actor`, `actor_plural`. Author's choice: "on commercial jobs" (the founders ask
   for introductions to commercial general contractors in [LYC]).

2. **What (the job).** Keep the record of the day's work, for liability and disputes.
   [HN] "30-200 photos per day to document site progress (mostly for liability reasons, or in case of a dispute with the
   owner over delays and deliverables)"; photos used to create "daily logs", "structured documents that account for the
   work done on site on any given day". [KOE] the log is "a critical piece of documentation in the arbitration of a
   dispute". → `statements.problem`, `context.job`, `interpretations.problem`.

3. **When / where.** At the end of the day, after the site walks, in the trailer.
   [HN] "At the end of the day, they'll spend a few hours uploading those photos into OneDrive, or project management
   software like Procore or ACC." [YCP] "We were curious what superintendents were doing for hours in their trailers at
   the end of the day." [LYC] "supes are spending up to 3 hours a day creating documents". → `context.circumstance`, `occasion: daily log`.
   Author's choice: the recall window {5, WORKING_DAYS} and Frequency 4 to 5 working days out of 5 (the posts say "per
   day"; a five-day site week is assumed). Prevalence `p_80_100` ("Nearly all") follows from the same "per day".

4. **Which people (the comparable group).** Superintendents at US general contractors whose jobs run on Procore or ACC.
   [LYC] "210k+ construction superintendents ... across the USA"; "Project management tools like Procore and ACC have
   dramatically increased documentation requirements". [YCP] "driving to Napa, South Bay, and around SF". → `context.segment`,
   `market: US`.

5. **Who pays.** The general contractor, per site.
   [HN] "we charge per site per month, which includes unlimited users on any given construction project".
   → `persona.decision_maker: {role: contractor}`, the BUYER role. Author's choice: the decider is the contractor's
   "operations lead" and the role to test is "The CFO" (a second role, "The project executive", listed); Purchase
   friction's three steps ("A trial on one live job" tested, a Procore check, a security review) and Commitment's step
   "start a paid pilot on one site" are the author's. Public material names no buyer title; [LYC] asks for
   introductions to general contractors by firm, not by role.

6. **Mechanism.** Narrated short videos turned into notes, texted to the crew, pushed to Procore/ACC.
   [HN] "Supers simply take short videos with voiceover, or upload photos, and Fresco does the rest, creating notes with
   transcription, photos, assignees, and due dates. Supers can easily text their crew action items, and receive texts
   back". "We also route this to whatever project management software they're using with a single click."
   [LYC] the narrated example "The beam in the southwest corner of room 134 is corroded and needs replacement by Alex.";
   "Supes who use Fresco complete their notes, on average, 90% faster."
   → `statements.solution`, `solution_mechanism`, Compatibility and Adoption friction items. Relative advantage's two
   benefits are from [HN] ("during their site walks, not after") and [LYC] ("90% faster"); their wording is the author's.

7. **Price.** About $1k per site per month, less with multi-site or multi-month terms.
   [HN] "The typical price is $1k/month, but we offer discounts for multi-month or multi-site commitments."
   → `commercial.price` {800, 1000, month}. Author's choice: the low end of $800 stands for the stated discounts.
   Existing sacrifice: 30 to 60 hours a month per site at an hourly rate of 55 — from [LYC] "up to 3 hours a day" and
   [HN] "a few hours uploading", taken as 1.5 to 3 hours on about twenty working days (author's arithmetic). The rate is
   [BLS] "$55.28 per hour" (median, construction managers, May 2025), the author's stand-in: no superintendent wage is
   in the public material. Ability to pay is derived by code (24% to 61%).

8. **Occasions.** The narrated beam; a school refit report; the uploads and logs at the end of the day.
   [LYC] on a school refit walkthrough: "Normally, creating the final report takes 2+ hours."
   [HN] "few supers have time to do this thoroughly, so these photos aren't very searchable." No named customer quote
   exists in public; the occasions below are scripted from these and from practitioner comments.

No respondent carries the name of a commenter, customer or founder.

## Open
- The verdict was scripted to be plausible and not obviously "build": the problem holds on how often but people
  disagree on whether the log is one of their two worst difficulties; the solution splits on the benefit and on
  talking over videos on site; the price fails (two of eight at the founder's band or above) while the cost it would
  replace is above the price. This is the author's reading of the thread's sceptics, not a measured result.
- No public account names a buyer title at a general contractor; the decider, the tested role "The CFO", the purchase
  steps and the Commitment step are the author's.
- hourly_rate 55 is a proxy (construction managers, not superintendents).
- Existing sacrifice picks use `period: quarter` (the corpus's convention), although the registry's recall period for a
  monthly cost reads "last month"; the values are the monthly figures times three.
- The window {5, WORKING_DAYS} is the author's; the public posts say "per day".

screens.why1: Right after I checked the three start-up efforts Keel wrote, it's obvious I now have to pick the one my supers are most likely to balk at, since they only get one question on it.
screens.why2: Short videos with voiceover on site walks, checking the notes before they go out, hooking it to Procore or ACC: these are my own words and my supers' words, readable at a glance.
screens.why3: I've watched supers on walks in Napa and the South Bay and heard the pushback, so I know the real sticking point is talking into a phone in front of the crew, not the Procore hookup.
screens.why4: The three efforts are the ones I gave, distinct and complete for what a super has to do to start; the Procore/ACC link is usually set up by the GC's admin rather than the super, but it still belongs on the list as the founder's choice.
screens.why5: The belief and the test say exactly what I meant, 'most would take short videos and talk over them on walks', with no product name or buyer role leaking into what the super will see.

screens.why1: Right before the study goes out is the obvious place to decide whether to collect emails from people who want to try Fresco on a real job.
screens.why2: "Offer a pilot?" with "Yes, ask them / No pilot" is plain to me, and the hint shows the exact line people will see.
screens.why3: Whether I want pilot leads is my own call as the founder, and I can answer it at once.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it, the two options are distinct, and no escape is needed for a founder's own choice.
screens.why5: My commitment step was "start a paid pilot on one site" with the contractor, but the generic "Would you try this for real? Leave your email" drops the paid, one-site part and doesn't say whether supers or the contractor's ops lead get the line.
screens.instead: Offer a pilot? People who say yes see: "Would you try this on one of your live jobs? Leave your email." (Yes, ask them / No pilot)

screens.why1: Choosing who asks my superintendents the questions belongs right before the link goes out, after the pilot offer.
screens.why2: The question is plain, but the hint says the interviewer appears on video yet offers only voices to hear, so I have to read it twice to know whether I am picking a face, a voice or both, and why 400 credits is charged to record it.
screens.why3: Picking who speaks to my own supes is my call, and I can judge it by listening to the samples.
screens.why4: Two named interviewers with a 5-second sample each is complete for a choice of interviewer, Daphne is preselected, and the cost is the same either way, so no escape is needed.
screens.why5: It says 'construction superintendents' as I typed it and shows nothing of Fresco to them; the text-message link matches how I reach my crews.
screens.instead: Who should ask construction superintendents your questions on video? Hear each one; the same 400 credits either way. [Daphne ▶ 5 s] [Saskia ▶ 5 s]

screens.why1: After choosing who asks the questions, deciding how my supers will answer is the natural next step before sending.
screens.why2: AI interviewer, read and tap, let them choose are plain to me as a founder building an AI product.
screens.why3: I know my supers are on loud sites with phones in hand, so I can pick a format from what I know of them.
screens.why4: The three options cover the field, but the Daphne option crams in a recording status and noise claims that read as setup noise rather than a choice, and Let them choose waits on Daphne.
screens.why5: It names my actor as I typed it and leaks nothing of Fresco into the respondent's side.
screens.instead: How should construction superintendents answer? Options: AI interviewer (talk to Daphne, ready in a few minutes) / Read and tap (ready now) / Let them choose (ready when Daphne is)

screens.why1: After choosing how supers answer, deciding who gets the link is the obvious last step before sending.
screens.why2: The three choices read plainly to me as a founder, and the 'Contacts page' points at a part of Keel I've used.
screens.why3: I know whether I'm sending to supers I've met on Bay Area jobsites or posting in a group, so this is mine to answer.
screens.why4: The options are distinct and cover my cases, but the open-link option forces a Google sign-in that a lot of field supers on their phones won't have handy, and nothing says how many links or whether I can mix sources.
screens.why5: Nothing of my product leaks and my pick, people I know by name, is kept as typed.
screens.instead: Who gets a link? -- Supers I know by name (one link each) / A list I found with Keel / One open link I post where supers already are (they sign in with Google or a phone number)

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' is stated with '4 answered' beside it, but the deciding threshold (5 needed) only appears on the cards, and it is unexplained why 4 of the 7 who answered counted on every card.
screens.why_b2: There is no chart here; the cards read '4 answered · 5 needed to call it', which shows the count and the bar, but the kicker's '7 people answered' against '4 answered' on each card needs a second look to reconcile.
screens.why_b3: All three dimension names and belief lines are exactly the ones I checked on the way in, from talking over the noise to hours back at the end of the day.
screens.why_b4: Nothing tells me what to do: not whether to send the study to more superintendents, how many more, or whether the 4 answers lean one way.
screens.why_b5: It refuses to call anything on 4 answers and keeps n visible, though the restated solution sentence under the title is garbled and repeats itself.
screens.instead: Too few to call: of the 7 who answered, only 4 superintendents reached the solution questions, and you need 5 per belief, so send the study to at least 1 more super on a live commercial job to get a verdict on each.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside the number that decides it, '4 answered · 5 needed to call it', and the So line says the same.
screens.why_b2: The bars and the 4 counted are plain, but the bar label 'your bar · 3 of 4' sits next to 'no more than 1 in 3 say only sometimes or no', and the grey ghost cell for Luis takes a second look before I see that 3 of 4 is where I'd clear it.
screens.why_b3: Compatibility and 'they could talk over the noise on site' are the name and line I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: 'Ray's no is the one to ask about' points at someone but not at what to do; it doesn't tell me to get one more counted answer, try Luis again for a real occasion, or ask about noise on site directly.
screens.why_b5: n stays visible and it is called a lean, not a call, but the card files a general 'would it have fitted the way things were set up' answer under my noise belief; nobody was asked about noise, and the quote shown is about the log waiting till morning, not about noise.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 3 of 4 say it would have fitted their last log and 1 more answer decides it, but no one was asked about talking over site noise, so ask Ray what didn't fit and ask the next super whether they could narrate over the noise on the deck.

screens.why_b1: The verdict 'Too few to call' sits right beside the number that decides it, '4 answered · 5 needed to call it', so I know why no call was made.
screens.why_b2: I can see it counts 4 supers, 3 'a lot better' against 1 'no difference', but the bar label '3 of 4 (no more than 1 in 3 say no difference or worse)' mixes a for-count with an against-rule, and the ghost cell for Luis takes a second look to place.
screens.why_b3: The title and the belief line, 'hours back at the end of the day', are the ones I checked going in.
screens.why_b4: 'Nothing is settled here yet' is generic: it doesn't tell me that one more counted superintendent would settle it, or that the lean is toward holding.
screens.why_b5: It keeps n visible, says outright that a small group is 'a lean, not a call', excludes Luis's guess, and doesn't dress 3 of 4 up as a result.
screens.instead: Too few to call: 4 counted, 5 needed. 3 of 4 say a lot better, so it leans toward holding. One more superintendent's answer about their last daily log settles it. Denise, who logs on the tablet as she goes, saw no gain; her real pain is the schedule and the subs.

screens.why_b1: "Too few to call" sits right beside the deciding number, 4 counted against 5 needed, and the So line repeats it.
screens.why_b2: The bars and the strip (3 for, 1 against, 1 ghost) are clear, but "your bar · 3 of 4" reads like the result rather than the threshold, so I had to work out that 1 in 4 against is under my 1-in-3 bar.
screens.why_b3: Adoption friction and "Most would take short videos and talk over them on walks" are exactly what I checked on the way in.
screens.why_b4: "Nothing is settled here yet" is generic: it doesn't say one more counted answer settles it, or that it leans toward holding while two of my three yeses are conditional.
screens.why_b5: The heading says "4 answered" but the count line says 5 answered and 4 counted, since Luis answered and was set aside, so the headline undercounts who replied; the small-n caution itself is honest.

screens.why_b1: Each box opens on "Too few to call" with "4 answered · 5 needed to call it" right beside it, so I know there is no verdict yet and exactly why.
screens.why_b3: Both dimension names and both belief lines are word for word the ones I checked on the way in (talk over the noise on site; hours back at the end of the day).
screens.why_b4: "5 needed to call it" implies I should get more superintendents to answer, but the screen never says so, and it never says what the two against answers mean for the idea.
screens.why_b5: The n stays visible on every box, the low n is named as too few to call, and the single quotes are labelled as one person each, with no claim beyond them.
screens.why_b6: Both quotes tell me something I did not type: when the day is on fire the log slides to the next morning rather than eating the trailer hours, and for Denise the log is done on the tablet before she leaves the gate, while the schedule and getting subs to show up are what eat the day.

screens.why1: As the first screen it makes sense to check whether my jobs even run on something like Procore before asking about my daily logs.
screens.why2: Nobody on my site says 'cloud construction management system' -- I'd say Procore or ACC, so I'd pause a second to be sure that's what they mean.
screens.why3: I know exactly what my jobs are set up on, so I can answer this straight.
screens.why4: Yes or no covers it cleanly for a gate question, and a gate carries no escape.
screens.why5: It keeps the founder's Procore-or-ACC segment, but the generic category label reads like a vendor's word rather than mine.
screens.why6: It's one short question, but 'cloud construction management system' is a mouthful heard once, and 'I'll read 2 options' for a plain yes or no sounds stiff.
screens.instead: Is any job you're running now set up in Procore, ACC or something like them? Yes or no.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether my job runs on Procore, asking whether I did my own daily log this week is the obvious next thing to check before asking me to walk through it.
screens.why2: 'Type up by hand' trips me up, because by hand to me means pen and paper, yet it says type, so I'm not sure whether entering it in Procore myself counts.
screens.why3: I write the daily log nearly every day I'm on site, so I know straight off whether I did one this week.
screens.why4: Yes and No cover it, but the chips are odd: 'I can't recall one particular daily log' makes no sense for a yes-or-no about this week, and 'I'd rather not say' on whether I did my log is strange.
screens.why5: Keeping the day's record still comes through, but 'by hand' hints that someone is setting me up against an automated way of doing it, which drifts from simply writing up the day's photos and notes.
screens.why6: Said aloud it's one short question ending in 'Yes or no', easy to answer on one hearing.
screens.instead: In the last 5 working days, did you write up a daily log yourself from your photos and notes? Yes · No

screens.why1: Part 1 asked about my daily log and how I get it typed up, so showing the idea before part 2 is the obvious next step.
screens.why2: Most of it is plain to me, but the last sentence, 'take your site walk from short videos you talk over to notes', took a second read, and 'scribe' isn't a word anyone on site uses.
screens.why3: I walk the site, take photos, assign items to subs and push it all into Procore, so I can picture exactly how this would fit my day.
screens.why4: A card to read, with no options.
screens.why5: Part 1 was about the daily log, but the card talks about site walk notes and crew action items, which is closer to punch lists than the daily log I fill out, so it drifted a little.
screens.why6: It can be said, but it's five sentences, and the closing belief sentence repeats the how in a clumsy shape that is hard to follow when heard once.
screens.instead: Imagine Fresco, an AI scribe for site walks. You take short videos on your walk and talk over them; it turns them into notes with photos, who owns each item and when it's due, texts the crew their items, and sends the notes to Procore or ACC in one click. The people building it believe it would save you the hours of typing up after the walk.

screens.why1: Right after the idea card, asking whether it would fit how my job is run is the obvious next thing to ask a super.
screens.why2: The 'it' could be Fresco or my daily log, and 'the way things were set up' doesn't say whether it means Procore, my company's log template or the owner's reporting, so I'd read it twice.
screens.why3: I know my Procore daily log setup cold, but I've never touched Fresco, so whether it would slot in is partly a guess from a one-line card.
screens.why4: 'Most of the time' and 'only sometimes' read like a frequency scale for a single daily log, so they don't line up well with one occasion, though 'I can't tell' fits.
screens.why5: Nothing of the product leaks, but 'the way things were set up' has drifted from what is surely meant, getting the notes and photos into the Procore or ACC daily log.
screens.why6: Short, one question, four short options and one escape, easy to hold when heard once.
screens.instead: Think of your last daily log. Could notes and photos from Fresco have gone straight into it in Procore? Yes; yes, with some steps; or no. Or say you can't tell.

screens.why1: Right after asking whether it would have fitted my setup, it's natural to ask whether it would actually have made my last daily log easier.
screens.why2: Daily log, a lot better, no difference: those are words I use on the job, and I get it on one read.
screens.why3: I typed up my last daily log a few days ago, so I can judge whether something for site walk notes and photos would have saved me the evening uploading.
screens.why4: A lot better, a little better, no difference and worse cover it without overlap, and 'I can't tell' fits if the card didn't tell me enough.
screens.why5: The card line 'site walk notes with photos' says less than the idea did, and it never says it's AI writing the log for me, so it reads like just another photo app.
screens.why6: One short question and four short options, said as a list I can hold, with one escape at the end.

screens.why1: After asking whether it fits my setup and whether it would have helped, asking whether I'd actually do what it takes to use it is the obvious last question.
screens.why2: Short videos, talking over them, site walks: those are the words I'd use myself, and I get it on one read.
screens.why3: I walk the job every day with my phone out, so I know whether I'd narrate video while I walk.
screens.why4: 'Yes' and 'Yes, if it was clearly worth it' partly overlap, since nobody says yes to something that isn't worth it, but the range is complete and 'I can't tell' fits.
screens.why5: The card above says 'site walk notes with photos' while the question says I'd be shooting video, so I'm left wondering whether it's photos or video.
screens.why6: One short question, four short options I can hold, and one escape said last.
screens.instead: To use Fresco, you'd take short videos and talk over them on your walks. Would you do that, or not? Yes · Yes, if it saved me time · Probably not · No · I can't tell
